As the depth (x) increases from the surface of the Earth, the value of r decreases, and hence the acceleration due to gravity decreases with increasing depth. It can be expressed as g' < g. From the obtained relation, the value of g decreases as the depth increases.
Note: At the center of the Earth, when x = R and r = 0, g' = 0, thus the weight of a body at the center, mg', is zero.
Moreover, g goes on decreasing in the either case and it becomes maximum on the surface of the Earth.

Fig 7.10: Variation of g with distance from the centre of the Earth 7.9 Center of Mass and center of Gravity 7.9.1 Center of Mass The center of mass is a representative point in a rigid body where whole of the mass of the body is supposed to be concentrated. A rigid body consists of large number of tiny particles of individual masses m1, m2, ….,mn, and so on. The sum of the masses of all these particles constitutes the mass of the body. The center of mass is a point where a force can be applied to produce the same linear motion as the motion of the entire body. The force acting upon this point produces linear acceleration but no angular motion.
